Not with a consensus (clearly) nor with any authority, for English. It's all just what various users say it should be, and/or how users of the language use it, depending on whether you've more of prescriptivist or descriptivist inclination. In both cases, though, it comes from the users of the language, none of whom can claim any sort of authority over the others. Ergo, it's explicitly self-centered and technically incorrect to claim that the English grammar rules one follows are the OneTrueSet for everyone - just as it would be incorrect to assert that the way one brushed one's teeth was the only correct way to do it.

The only metric for what is and isn't acceptable English is literally which constructions its speakers accept - and at the moment the singular "they" is accepted by many and rejected by many, as well. With no consensus among English speakers, it cannot be called fully incorrect, nor can it be called fully correct (though the long usage history w/out complaint tends to lend credence to the latter position).

This is not the case for all languages. There are many languages with an official regulating body - and of course, most constructed languages will be similarly prescribed. In these cases, it can be determined, with the finality that comes from authority, whether a given construction in the language is correct or incorrect.

It is not a repeater it is different:

WiFi backscatter PDF: https://homes.cs.washington.edu/~gshyam/Papers/wifibackscatter.pdf

You still need your normal powered wifi (T1) that is your transmitter. This radio energy gets absorbed by the passive Wifi device (P1) and used as energy source. Now here comes the key, a second wifi device listens (L1) to T1, but the P1 device will either absorb the T1 energy or not absorb the T1 energy so that the L1 device will detect a very tiny variation in T1 energy. And that is the information.

The equivalent would be that you put a loud speaker in one room (T1), and a microphone at another room (L1) and the passive wifi device (P1) would open or close a shutter somewhere in the room that cause more or less absorption of the sound.

Or another way to see it could be a light (T1) in one place and a light detector (L1) in another place and you have a device (P1) that absorbs more or less light. And P1 gets powered by the light of T1.
